claim: Sampling/execution-based (self-consistency) confidence is well-calibrated and discriminative for code functional correctness (AUROC ~0.80-0.99 across studies).
note: This is now 2026 CONSENSUS. It is therefore NOT a novel headline by itself — the paper must build ON it, not re-establish it.

claim: Token log-probability is a poor predictor of code functional correctness; post-hoc calibration improves ECE but not discrimination.
note: Settled ground; can assert without hedging.

claim: Every existing train-time method for making STATED/verbalized confidence calibrated has been evaluated on QA/math/reasoning, NOT on code generation.
note: The load-bearing GAP. ~10+ independent methods, zero code. RLCM touches code only via OOD probe transfer, not code-specific expressed-confidence training.

claim: Distilling a self-consistency / sampling signal into a model's stated confidence (via SFT or RL) raises verbal discrimination substantially (AUROC to ~0.79-0.86) at 7-8B single-GPU scale.
note: Strong PRIOR EVIDENCE that the proposed mechanism works => underwrites P2 (confidence the headline lands). The novelty is porting it to code with execution-grounded targets.

claim: Uncertainty signals, once available, translate into real downstream wins for code (decoding-time gains +16-21% pass@1; abstention with formal risk control).
note: Supports a utility/selective-generation corollary; AAAI precedent exists (AdapT @ AAAI 2024).

claim: Deployed single-pass/post-hoc confidence interfaces fail to help real developers, and developers prefer coarse/categorical signals over raw numbers.
note: Motivation for a BETTER expressed interface; licenses a categorical/risk-tier output.
